head.name: @fzlt/core/beam
head.lead: Lasers on a board. Parts (mirrors, splitters, blockers, targets, emitters) stand on a flat board plane in board coordinates [x, z], free or on a grid; run() casts every emitter's ray, reflecting off mirrors at any angle, passing through and splitting at splitters, stopping at blockers, targets and the board's edge, and writes the segments and hits into fixed typed arrays. - A part is a segment (len, turned by a) or a circle (r). Angles are radians from +x toward +z; on a diorama an object turned to angle a has rot[1] = −a. Multiples of π/4 take exact directions (no Math.cos rounding), so a grid puzzle traces the same bits in every browser. - Deterministic: the same parts give the same segments in the same order (depth first, the transmitted ray before the reflected one). bounces caps the turns on one path (capped counts the paths it stopped), segs the segments (dropped counts the rest). - dioramaBeam draws the result on an @fzlt/core/diorama board: glowing beams as decals in the depth sort (split into short pieces so they sort among the parts), a pulse of points along them, sparks where a beam hits a target or a blocker; a re-routed beam grows out from where it changed. No allocation per run() or show() in the steady state. 2D lengths use steer's exact hypot.

sizesNote: Measured on this build: minified and gzipped with everything it imports, the way npm run size checks the budget in CI.
